Cerebras Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:CBRS) faces more potential selling when up to 19.4 million more shares become eligible for sale on Wednesday under the AI chipmaker’s staggered IPO lock-up.

The stock is on watch after sliding 10.7% to $146.62 on Monday, its lowest close yet, according to Benzinga Pro market data. Shares are down about 58% from their $350 opening price in May and trade roughly 21% below the $185 IPO price.

  • CBRS stock is moving. See the real-time price action here. 

Lock-Up Clock Ticks

Cerebras set up its lock-up to release insider stock in stages rather than all at once, similar to SpaceX. The releases were planned in several rounds running through the end of October, Axios reported at the time of the IPO.

The last tranche of this size arrived Sept. 30. Up to 19.4 million shares held by directors, officers, employees and other holders unlocked that day, equal to 8% of shares outstanding. The stock fell 8.9% that day.

Before that, up to 14.6 million shares had been freed every two weeks since Aug. 19.

Insiders have been selling. CEO Andrew Feldman and CTO Sean Lie sold more than $240 million of Class A shares between Aug. 20 and Sept. 25 under trading plans, according to Benzinga’s insider sale data. 

Read Also: SpaceX Stock Faces Another Wave of Insider Shares

OpenAI Doubts Linger

The unlock comes on top of questions about Cerebras’ biggest customer. On Sept. 30, research firm SemiAnalysis said OpenAI would run the “Ultrafast” mode of GPT-6.1 Sol on NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) GPUs rather than on Cerebras hardware. Cerebras fell nearly 20% that week and closed at $166.43 on Oct. 2.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman pushed back late that Friday. 

“There is some speculation about our partnership with Cerebras. Cerebras is a close partner, and we have a deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed,” he wrote on X. The stock jumped 9% the following Monday. His post did not say which chips run the new tier.

Citi analysts said their 2026-2028 revenue outlook for Cerebras was “unchanged.” They called it “too early to read much into” the rollout, CNBC reported. 

The two companies are closely tied. Cerebras has a multiyear deal worth more than $20 billion to supply OpenAI with 750 megawatts of computing power. OpenAI also lent Cerebras $1 billion and holds warrants for up to 33.4 million shares.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Altman Bounce Fades

Cerebras’ Altman bounce didn’t hold. Shares have fallen about 19% since closing at $181.55 on Oct. 5.

Pressure across the sector added to the losses. AI stocks slid Oct. 8 after reports that OpenAI’s annualized revenue at the end of September was about $18 billion below earlier figures. 

On Monday, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) unveiled its Maia 300 chip and said it would become the main inference system for Microsoft’s own products. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 2.7% the same day. 

Inference is the core of Cerebras’ pitch, and each new in-house chip from a big cloud company makes the competitive question harder to ignore.

Cerebras is now worth about $34.8 billion. It was valued near $95 billion after its first day of trading.

Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) stock is slightly up on Tuesday during a broader sell-off in semiconductor stocks, growing concerns about the sustainability of AI spending and the lingering effect of last week’s legal dispute with Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM).

The Nasdaq is down 0.56% while the S&P 500 has shed 0.13%, and Technology is also in the red (down 0.6%).

•  Where is ARM Holdings stock headed?

AI Buildout and Capital Constraints

Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) CEO Hock Tan spoke at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference in Singapore on Monday. "A lot of investors have no clue what they’re investing in, but set very extreme expectations, only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino gambling," Tan said, according to Reuters. Tan also said, "[What] I think might be the biggest constraint is capital."

Brookings Institution research published in September projects the U.S. AI infrastructure buildout will reach $10.3 trillion through 2032, averaging 3.63% of U.S. GDP annually.

Qualcomm Trial Adds to Arm’s Pressure

Separately, a Delaware jury received Qualcomm’s lawsuit against Arm on Friday, Reuters reported. Qualcomm alleges Arm breached its licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged Qualcomm’s dealings with Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META). The five-day federal trial in Wilmington is the second legal proceeding between the companies in two years. Qualcomm’s architecture license with Arm extends through 2033.

From a longer-term trend view, ARM is still holding above its 200-day SMA ($221.53), but the stock is now trading 13.5% below its 20-day SMA ($290.20) and 7.2% below its 50-day SMA ($270.41), which frames the recent move as a pullback inside a bigger uptrend. The bigger-picture trend markers are mixed but still constructive: the Golden Cross in April (50-day SMA over the 200-day SMA) keeps the longer-term bias tilted higher, even as the stock works off the September swing high. With the 52-week high set in June ($452.70) and the 52-week low in February ($100.02), ARM remains volatile, so traders tend to anchor on nearby moving-average levels for direction.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) is expanding its AI strategy beyond consumer products and advertising as it targets developers and enterprise customers with new models and business tools.

BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones maintains a positive view on Meta with an $885 price forecast, implying 23% upside from the Oct. 9 price of $718.70.

Muse Wonder Broadens Meta’s AI Push

Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its latest AI models. The company said the models match or exceed the capabilities of current frontier models.

Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers. Meta also plans to use Muse Wonder to power Meta Muse, initially for paid subscribers.

Jones said the launch strengthens Meta’s position in the competition among leading AI developers.

He said the models primarily target developers and enterprises, supporting Meta’s broader effort to expand into business customers following the creation of Meta Enterprise Platform.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Jones Sees Long-Term Monetization Beyond Ads

Jones said Meta’s rapid pace of product launches creates another path to monetize its AI investments outside its core advertising business.

BNP Paribas said the near- to medium-term revenue contribution from Muse Wonder and other recent products remains unclear.

However, Jones believes Meta can generate enough long-term revenue from these products to support its substantial AI spending.

The firm is now looking to Meta’s third-quarter earnings call for early adoption trends.

Jones also plans to monitor third-party data to determine whether the new models are increasing engagement and usage of Meta Muse.

BNP Paribas’ $885 price forecast leaves Jones constructive on Meta’s longer-term ability to convert AI investment into additional revenue, even though the timing and size of near-term contributions remain uncertain.

Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones is betting oil could rise another $25 a barrel and warning that 2027 could be a “really, really challenging” year for stocks.

“Long oil, bullish on oil, I think it can rally another 20 or 25 bucks,” the Tudor Investment Corp. founder told CNBC Tuesday.

Asked how stocks would react, he replied: “Well, it’ll hate it. Absolutely totally hate it.”

Why Jones Is Bullish on Oil

Jones suspects President Donald Trump could take a tougher approach to Iran after the Nov. 3 midterm elections. If a softer solution existed, he argued, it would likely have emerged by now.

“It’s kind of like the sword of Damocles sitting over the oil market post the midterms,” Jones said, acknowledging he had no inside knowledge of Trump’s plans.

Trump said last Thursday the U.S. would not attack Iran before the elections, while Tehran has been preparing for renewed hostilities.

WTI crude traded near $94 Tuesday. A $20-to-$25 increase would take it to roughly $114-$119, although Jones did not specify a benchmark or deadline.

On Kalshi, traders put the chance of WTI settling above $115 before December 31 at around 33%, and above $120 at 26%.

Kalshi and Benzinga have an existing data collaboration agreement.

A Strong Fourth Quarter Before a Tough 2027?

Jones sees a strong fourth-quarter rally as “very possible” based on historical midterm-election patterns, which often see stocks bottom in late October or early November.

But he compared today’s AI-driven, “two-speed” market to 1999, when technology stocks surged before the dot-com crash.

“2027 is going to be really, really challenging for the stock market,” he warned.

His concern is less about valuations than about the supply of shares. Buybacks and acquisitions have supported stocks for years by reducing available shares, but IPOs and insider sales could reverse that trend.

“You’ve probably got the most negative flow picture for the U.S. stock market that we’ve had say since 2002,” Jones said.

Jones cited SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), which went public in June but still has billions of shares held by insiders and early investors restricted from sale until 2027.

He also pointed to potential IPOs from Anthropic and OpenAI. Jones fears the combination of new listings and insider share sales could overwhelm investor demand, pushing stock prices lower.

Goldman Sachs forecasts $600 billion in new stock issuance next year, while another $1.7 trillion in previously restricted shares could become eligible for sale. The bank says the resulting increase in stock supply could be the largest since 2000.

However, Goldman expects $1.7 trillion in corporate buybacks and believes many newly unlocked shares won’t actually be sold. Unlike Jones, the bank expects the stock market rally to continue.

The United States Oil Fund (NYSE:USO) rose about 0.7% late Tuesday morning, while SpaceX shares fell nearly 4% and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) edged lower.

Jordi Visser does not think Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) is close to its earnings peak.

Yet, he would still rather put new money somewhere else.

The head of AI Macro Nexus Research at 22V Research told Benzinga in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that he bought Micron shares over the past three months, as the stock fell below $1,000.

The position is smaller than the one he sold in May. Now, his favorite areas are optics companies and crypto.

Visser Sees No Earnings Peak for Micron

Micron was down 5.5% at $934 on Tuesday afternoon, on track for a fourth straight decline. It trades 23% below its June 25 record close.

In Seoul, SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) dropped 10.1% and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (OTC:SSNLF) lost 7.4%.

The pressure came from China.

ChangXin Memory Technologies, known as CXMT, expects to launch a denser server memory product around year-end, the South China Morning Post reported. More supply could ease the shortage behind record memory profits.

"I do not think we are close to an earnings peak for Micron," he said.

He expects a memory cycle to "eventually play out," but not in the next couple of years.

Read Also: SK Hynix Stock Falls Below 200-Day Average: A Chinese Rival’s IPO Filing May Explain Why

Why Visser Prefers Optics and Crypto

Even so, his Micron position will not be as large as it was six months ago.

"I think there are better places to put money for the next year," Visser said.

"I am focused on the rise of personal/consumer agents now and the beginning of the Vera Rubin data center platform," he added.

Vera Rubin is the next generation of AI data center hardware from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

"This leaves me with optics companies and crypto (financial guardrails for AI commerce) as my favorite areas going forward," Visser said.

Optics companies make the lasers and fiber links that move data inside AI data centers. Visser did not name individual stocks.

Among optical component makers, Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) and Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR) are up 156% and 51% this year.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) traded near $83,100, down 5% in 2026.

Why Record Profits Earn a Low Multiple

Micron reported record revenue of $54.23 billion for its fiscal fourth quarter, nearly five times the level of a year earlier.

Yet the stock trades at about 5.4 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2027, according to TradingView consensus data. The S&P 500 trades at 19.1 times, according to FactSet.

A low forward price-to-earnings multiple means investors doubt the profits will last.

Visser gave three reasons.

"Because memory has historically been cyclical, investors do expect that memory companies are going to hit that cyclical earnings peak soon," he said.

The second reason is the wider market. The S&P 500’s multiple was 22.2 in January.

Visser said that compression carries "a risk built in that some companies have a terminal value issue from AI competition." Terminal value is what investors assume a business will be worth many years from now.

The third is interest rates. The 10-year Treasury yield trades at 5.22%, after touching a 24-year high of 5.36% last week.

"With rates rising there is a growing fear that an AI bubble could pop," Visser said.

"All of this is about the uncertainty of where AI will be in the coming years," he added. "I expect this pressure to remain."

Memory Demand Has No Cliff, but Margins Will Fall

Visser compared memory to oil.

"We will need massive amounts for a long time," he said. "That does not mean that supply won’t catch up with demand."

"We need more oil every year and supply and demand is close to balance," he added.

In his view, an AI-driven advance, such as more efficient models, will eventually close the gap between memory supply and demand.

"I don’t think there is a cliff where memory demand drops but margins will certainly drop at some point," Visser said.

Micron’s gross margin, the share of revenue left after production costs, reached 86.8% last quarter.

His caution extends beyond memory.

"I have a very negative view on all public companies by 2030 based on AI impacting future certainty of all businesses regardless of what you do," he said.

Investor Ray Dalio warned that the United States faces a “death spiral” due to an oversupply of government debt. This structural imbalance is materializing as the U.S. Treasury struggles to contain rising yields despite escalating its bond buyback operations.

Supply Overwhelms Demand

Dalio outlined that countries go broke when the supply of debt surpasses demand and when debt service payments rise enough to “painfully squeeze out other spending.” He noted that both conditions are currently occurring in the U.S.

According to Dalio, increased debt pushes yields higher, which raises interest expenses and deficits, directly requiring even more debt issuance. Credit market participants refer to this compounding cycle as a “death spiral.”

Read Also: Scott Bessent Says ‘I Am the House Now’ and Dares Traders to Bet Against Him — Wall Street Fires Back With ‘Activist Treasury’ Label

The Bond Market Fights the Treasury

Dalio’s warnings align with recent Treasury market friction. In September, the U.S. Treasury tripled its long-term bond buyback operations to a $6 billion maximum to support market liquidity.

Despite this intervention, the 10-year Treasury yields climbed to multi-year highs. Market commentators like The Kobeissi Letter noted that “the bond market is quite literally fighting the US Treasury,” warning that consumers and borrowers are “in for a rude awakening” if yields continue their ascent past 5%.

Corporate Debt and Equities Face Pressure

Dalio projects that the federal government will issue $2.1 trillion in net new marketable debt over the full year of 2026. Furthermore, corporate debt and equity issuance are surging simultaneously, driven largely by artificial intelligence capital expenditures.

Dalio expects this combined wave of government and corporate issuance to create “too much supply of financial assets (both debt and equity) relative to the demand for it.”

While the economy is currently in a “mid-cycle” phase where rates have not yet crashed asset prices, Dalio anticipates that these sustained supply imbalances will eventually lead to economic weakness and negatively impact equity markets.

How Have the Stock and Bond Markets Performed?

At the last check, the 10-year Treasury bond yielded 5.20%, the 2-year Treasury bond yielded 4.78%, and the 30-year Treasury yielded 5.55%.

CoreWeave’s Soaring Yield

The ‘Private Credit Bubble’ Warning

According to his analysis, capital spending by major technology companies—Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL), and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX)—is projected to climb from $470 billion in 2025 to over $1.3 trillion by 2027.

Palihapitiya noted that debt, leases, and other financing methods are filling the massive funding gap. Direct lending to U.S. borrowers has grown rapidly, swelling from $96 billion in 2010 to roughly $2.4 trillion in 2025.

According to the charts shared by Palihapitiya in his X article, the tech firms alone account for $1.05 trillion, or 44%, of the total 2025 direct loan market. Within that sector, outstanding loans to software (SaaS) firms exceed $500 billion, representing 19% of direct loans, while loans directed specifically to AI, big-data, and cloud companies top $200 billion, or nearly 8% of the total.

Risks for Lenders and Borrowers

In his deep dive, Palihapitiya pointed out that lenders appear to be charging very little extra for AI-related risks. He noted that private loans for AI companies carry an average spread of 6.2 percentage points above the base rate, compared to 6.1 percentage points for other private credit loans.

The investor cautioned that this minimal difference in loan pricing suggests lenders may be underestimating the dual risks of AI: the technology could take too long to generate revenue for its builders, or it could rapidly disrupt the legacy software companies that currently dominate private credit portfolios.

Memory and semiconductor rivals SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY), Western Digital Corp. (NASDAQ:WDC), Seagate Technology Holdings Plc. (NASDAQ:STX) also joined the selloff.

Cramer Says Selloff Overstates Micron’s China Risk

CNBC’s Jim Cramer said semiconductor stocks have traded increasingly as a group, with weakness in South Korea’s SK Hynix spilling into U.S. chip names such as Micron.

Cramer dismissed fears that growing competition from Chinese memory chipmakers could hurt Micron, calling the concerns “nonsense.” He argued that investors may be overlooking Micron’s underlying demand and customer commitments.

Cramer told on Wednesday that Micron has 26 long-term customer agreements covering revenue through 2030 and is negotiating contracts for 2031.

He rejected the idea that Chinese competition alone could undermine Micron’s outlook, saying major U.S. customers would have concerns about using Chinese memory.

Cramer also pointed to growing memory requirements across consumer devices and AI-related products as a reason to focus on end demand rather than the semiconductor index.

Pettit Says Memory Story Is in Transition

Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit said investors often struggle with stocks whose growth stories are shifting.

“Markets are interesting. They don’t really like stock stories that are in transition, and that’s where memory is right now,” Pettit said.

He told CNBC on Tuesday that memory previously benefited from strong earnings revisions, but investors now want companies to prove how durable that growth can be.

Pettit said pullbacks on negative headlines therefore make sense, even while fundamentals in large AI-related companies remain strong.

He also warned that elevated interest rates leave the broader market with limited room for disappointment.

Luria Says China Risk Is Already in the Math

D.A. Davidson Head of Technology Research Gil Luria said semiconductor results and outlooks across the AI supply chain have remained consistently positive.

“Results have gotten better, outlooks have gotten better, visibility has gotten better,” Luria said.

He acknowledged to CNBC on Wednesday that China’s CXMT has gained DRAM market share and continues to improve its technology, but said investors should distinguish between lower-end memory and high-bandwidth memory.

Luria said Chinese suppliers do not currently participate in the high-bandwidth memory market and cannot sell to major U.S. customers including Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) and NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

He said any near-term competitive effect from Chinese suppliers would therefore fall more heavily on SK Hynix and Samsung than Micron. Luria also said China itself remains undersupplied.

“When Micron says that the tightness is going to get worse next year and even worse the year after that, they are fully aware of what CXMT is developing, their product roadmap, what they have, what they don’t have, and that’s incorporated into their outlook,” he said.

The debate leaves investors balancing near-term volatility and China-related concerns against tight memory supply, AI demand and Micron’s longer-term customer contracts.

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares reached a record of $348.15 on Tuesday following the announcement of a home hardware lineup, before pulling back to close at $341.27.

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster stated the devices show Apple’s “product velocity is increasing,” but the strategy “misses the mark” on the artificial intelligence sector.

The Home View Unveiling

Apple introduced the Home View, a $299 display with a 7-inch screen designed to connect home accessories, email, and messaging. The launch is part of a broader ecosystem push that includes a $299 Apple TV with a remote-finding feature and a “Home Collection” of third-party accessories like locks and cameras.

Munster estimated Apple will sell around four million Home View devices. He projected this will add $1.5 billion to the company’s expected $525 billion revenue for fiscal 2027. He characterized this as an “incremental” gain, stating it would add roughly 1% to Apple’s total revenue.

The Generative AI Opportunity

Despite the hardware expansion, Munster cautioned that Apple is overlooking the larger shift toward generative AI. Speaking on the Pressure Points podcast, he argued that consumers face too much “friction” integrating smart home devices.

“I don’t think people are quite ready for that,” Munster said. “I think they’re ready for a lot of generative AI. I think they’re really ready for bots, for specialized bots.”

He concluded that the Home View “misses the mark, I think, relative to what the biggest opportunity is in consumer tech, which is around these personalized bots.”

Munster previously warned that Apple risks getting “boxed out of the services upside” if consumers lock into competitor AI workflows, such as Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Muse or Space Exploration Technologies Corp.‘s (NASDAQ:SPCX) Grokbot, at $20 a month.

Smartphone Demand

The stock’s intraday record also coincided with reports of increasing demand for Apple’s upcoming foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo. Apple reportedly increased supply chain orders for the device by 30%, taking initial supply estimates to 10 million units ahead of Oct. 16 preorders.

How Has AAPL Performed in 2026?

The stock was 0.44% higher in premarket trading on Wednesday. It was higher by 37.80% over the last year, up 25.35% year-to-date, and by 2.71% over the last month. The stock closed up 0.09% at $341.27 on Tuesday.

Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) Executive Chairman Michael Saylor says Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) will climb back above $100,000, even as his company stays willing to sell parts of its holdings.

Why Saylor Says Bitcoin’s Headwinds Are Turning Into Tailwinds

Saylor told Bloomberg Crypto Tuesday that Bitcoin recently bounced off its 200-week moving average and now trades at a 25% premium above it. 

He pointed to a favorable regulatory environment, accelerating bank adoption, and growing tokenized securities activity as factors shifting Bitcoin from headwinds into tailwinds.

Saylor argued AI spending is pulling capital away from traditional equities built on human labor, pushing investors instead toward scarce assets robots can’t replicate. 

He called Bitcoin “the king of commodities” in that environment, framing it as digital capital competing directly with gold and other scarce assets for investor dollars.

Why Strategy Sold Bitcoin This Summer Despite Saylor’s Hold-Forever Stance

Strategy sold a small amount of Bitcoin in June when it traded near $73,000, a move that broke from Saylor’s long-standing advice to never sell. 

Saylor described Strategy as a structured finance company that can buy or sell Bitcoin, dollars, equity, or credit on any given day to benefit shareholders.

He called the initial sale an “inoculation” moment that briefly spooked the market, pushing Bitcoin lower. 

Later Bitcoin sales of thousands of coins drew no reaction at all, and in one case the market actually traded up afterward, according to Saylor. 

He said locking into a permanent no-sell stance would ultimately hurt the company’s value rather than protect it.

Strategy has acquired more Bitcoin than any company in the world this year and expects that trend to continue as Bitcoin moves into what he calls a bull market. 

He said the company plans to keep issuing digital credit products like STRC alongside its Bitcoin purchases going forward.

How Saylor Breaks Down Investor Time Horizons

Saylor laid out a framework matching different investor needs to different products:

  • Need money within three months: money market funds.
  • Need money in three months to four years: STRC, which pays a 10% to 12% dividend.
  • No money needed for four-plus years, want lower risk: Bitcoin directly, targeting 20% to 30% annual returns.
  • Want to outperform Bitcoin: Strategy or Strive equity, amplified through credit issuance.

Why Saylor Thinks Strategy Beats Buying Bitcoin or ETFs Directly

Saylor said Bitcoin has returned roughly 38% annually since Strategy’s first purchase in August 2020, while MSTR stock has returned 52% to 53% annually over that same stretch, outperforming every major stock except Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). 

He argued Strategy’s ability to issue high-yield credit backed by its Bitcoin holdings, rather than just holding the asset directly, gives the company an edge no ETF or direct Bitcoin purchase can replicate.

AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton warned that increasingly advanced artificial intelligence (AI) could threaten humanity, urging stronger safeguards as he argued that humans must prioritize their own interests over potentially superintelligent machines.

Hinton Warns AI Could Threaten Humanity

On Tuesday, in an interview with The Guardian, Hinton, widely known as the "godfather of AI," warned that AI systems could eventually escape human control and pose an existential threat.

He estimated there was a 10% to 20% chance AI could cause human extinction in the coming decades.

"The unique problem with AI is that if it goes wrong, if it takes over, you don’t get a second chance," Hinton said.

Hinton also addressed criticism from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang, who dismissed his extinction-risk estimate as unscientific.

Hinton Slams Trump’s AI Stance, Says He Would ‘Choose Human Beings’

Hinton criticized President Donald Trump’s opposition to government safeguards for AI, calling him a "corrupt, senile felon."

He also argued that Trump’s use of the term "superintelligence" demonstrated a lack of understanding of AI.

"Superintelligence means smarter than people," Hinton said, adding that changing the terminology would not make AI more intelligent.

Describing advanced AI systems as "alien beings," Hinton noted that we should make them in a way that they are happy in a “symbiotic relationship” with humans “where our concerns are weighed more heavily than their concerns.”

"I’m willing to be selfish and choose human beings," he added.

Tech Leaders Embrace Superintelligence

First Lady Melania Trump renamed her annual student AI competition the Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge, aligning it with President Donald Trump’s push to replace the term AI with superintelligence, or SI.

Earlier this month, Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO Elon Musk said humanity serving as a "biological bootloader" for machine intelligence could be a successful outcome if superintelligence spread beyond Earth.

He described propagating superintelligence to the stars as a "great success condition."

In February, Meta Platforms, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang pushed back against concerns about screen addiction, saying the company’s vision of "personal superintelligence" focused on empowering users rather than keeping them online. He said the technology was intended to help people manage tasks, improve wellness, pursue goals and strengthen relationships.
